content: 1. The sanitary seawater intakes (sea chests) must be positioned forward of all overboard waste discharge outlets. These outlets include emergency and routine discharge lines from wastewater treatment facilities, bilge water, recreational water facilities, and ballast tanks. However, this does not apply to discharges from deck drains on open decks, cooling lines without chemical treatment, or alarmed vent/overflow pipes for gray water, treated gray or black water, and ballast tanks equipped with an automatic shutoff system for sanitary seawater intake. 2. Alarm systems for the above must be both visual and audible, and they must activate in a continuously occupied space. Similarly, alarmed emergency bilge discharge lines with an automatic shutoff system for sanitary seawater intake must also have visual and audible alarms that sound in a continuously occupied space. 3. Discharges from the anchor chain locker are permitted forward of the sea chest, provided the chain is rinsed or cleaned exclusively with seawater. 4. Alarmed vent/overflow pipes for heeling tanks and laundry water storage tanks with an automatic shutoff system for sanitary seawater intake are allowed. These alarms must also be visual and audible and must sound in a continuously occupied space. 5. Showers must be equipped to provide potable water at a temperature not exceeding 43°C (110°F) during normal operations. These showers must be installed within 10 meters of the entrances to recreational water facilities (RWFs). For facilities with multiple entrances, the location and number of showers will be determined during the plan review process. 6. Showers must be located within 10 meters of all entrances to each RWF. 7. For facilities that meet the definition of more than one type of RWF, the more protective turnover rate applies, which is 5 hours. 8. An automatic monitoring and recording system must be provided for free halogen residuals (in mg/L or ppm) and pH levels. This system must be capable of recording these levels 24 hours a day. Chart recorders or electronic data loggers with security features must be installed to record pH and halogen measurements. Electronic data loggers must record in increments of 15 minutes or less. The probe for the automated analyzer recorder must be installed before the compensation or make-up tank or from a line taken directly from the RWF. Appropriate sample taps must also be installed for analyzer calibration. 9. If potable water is introduced into RWFs with recirculated water after filtration and chemistry control, and the potable water combines with the RWF recirculation system, the potable water must be halogenated and pH-controlled to the level required for the RWF. This mixture may negatively impact the monitoring analyzer for the RWF. 10. If an activity pool has interactive RWF features such as flowing, misting, sprinkling, jetting, or waterfalls, a secondary disinfection system must be installed. 11. For children’s pools, secondary disinfection systems must include UV systems that allow for cleaning of the lamp jacket without disassembling the unit. The lamp must be accessible without requiring the disassembly of the entire unit. For example, it is acceptable if the lamp can be accessed for cleaning by removing fasteners or a cover. 12. For baby-only water facilities, a permanent, easy-to-read sign must be installed at each entrance. The letters on the sign must be at least 25 millimeters (1 inch) high. The sign must state the following: This facility is intended for use by children in diapers or children who are not completely toilet trained. Use of this facility may put children at increased risk for illness. Children with medical conditions that may increase their risk of illness should not use these facilities. Children experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhea, skin sores, or infections are prohibited from using these facilities. Children must wear a swim diaper. Children must be accompanied by an adult at all times. Ensure children have a clean swim diaper before using these facilities. Frequent swim diaper changes are recommended. Do not change diapers in the area of the baby-only water facility. A diaper-changing station has been provided (exact location to be specified) for your convenience. 13. The heading letters on the sign must be at least 26 millimeters (1 inch) high, while all other lettering must be at least 13 millimeters (1/2 inch) high.
